title: An isolate's arena is an ownership root, not an address range
scope:
what an isolate's *arena* is in this runtime, what one costs, what "released wholesale" runs,
and how a value crosses the boundary in each direction. It does not decide the `spawn script` surface,
the option names or failure-as-a-value — [0006](0006.md) owns all three — nor
the walk itself, which is [0023](0023.md) § 2 and lives in
`crates/nvs-runtime/src/graph.rs`. Enforcement of a byte cap is `[limits]`' and is goal `governance`'s, not this
ADR's; where the cap *attaches* is § 3 below.

summary.headline: A sandbox owns what it can reach, not a slab of memory
summary.body:
Entering a sandbox maps no memory and leaving one unmaps none. What the sandbox owns is
everything reachable from its own context, and the only way a value moves in or out is a copy at
the boundary. Tearing one down releases that whole tree and then sweeps the cycles the counts
could not free, running each object's proper cleanup. Because both sides allocate from the same
place, a value nothing else holds can cross by a plain handoff that costs nothing. A sandbox
never shares its parent's static variables.
